chunks: And from him, also, from Safwan, from 'Ula ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

One of the two Imams (peace be upon them) was asked about a man who enters Mecca after dawn or after Asr prayer. He said: 'He performs Tawaf and prays two Rak'ahs, provided it is not at the time of sunrise or at the time of its redness (sunset/dusk).'

And if the Tawaf is a voluntary Tawaf, then it is disliked to pray after it if he performed Tawaf after dawn or after Asr. And it is preferable to delay the prayer until after sunrise and after Maghrib. He narrated that.
ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim pray the two Rak'ahs after performing Tawaf in Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the temporal restrictions for the two Rak'ahs following the Tawaf al-Qudum, distinguishing between obligatory and voluntary contexts. It highlights the scholarly consensus on avoiding the specific times of *Karahat* (dislike) for prayer—sunrise and sunset—unless one is performing the specific Tawaf prayer, thereby linking ritual purity with precise temporal observance in Mecca.
